- Very close attention to detail

- Someone who enjoys owning the data and running a tight ship
- Proactive and positive, and genuinely happy doing admin

The long-term aim is for the successful candidate to become confident in managing payroll independently from start to finish. We welcome applications from local Thurrock residents, including individuals with lived experience and volunteers looking to progress into a Recovery Coordinator role within our drug and alcohol service. This is an excellent opportunity to develop skills, gain experience, and make a positive difference in supporting people on their recovery journey.

About the Role

As a Recovery Coordinator, you will play a vital role in supporting individuals aged 18 and over who are experiencing drug and alcohol-related challenges. Working within an integrated healthcare framework, you will deliver person-centred psychosocial interventions that empower individuals to make positive, sustainable changes and work towards their recovery goals.

You will manage a caseload of service users, undertaking comprehensive assessments, developing risk management plans and creating SMART care plans tailored to each individual's needs. Using a flexible approach that combines harm reduction and abstinence-based interventions, you will provide practical advice, guidance and structured support to help individuals improve their health, wellbeing and quality of life.

Your responsibilities will include delivering structured one-to-one interventions, facilitating group-work sessions and supporting structured treatment programmes. You will use motivational interviewing techniques to engage service users, encourage positive behaviour change and promote long-term recovery.

Building effective partnerships with housing providers, employment services, healthcare professionals, probation, the criminal justice sector and other community organisations will be essential to ensuring continuity of care and addressing the wider needs of the people you support.

You will contribute to service performance targets and positive outcomes, working collaboratively with colleagues, partner agencies and local commissioners to deliver high-quality, recovery-focused services. You will also maintain accurate records, participate in clinical supervision and ensure that safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion are embedded in your practice.

Flexibility is important, as the role may occasionally require evening or weekend working, with reasonable notice, to meet service user needs and maintain continuity of care.

About You

You are a compassionate, motivated and recovery-focused professional with experience of working within substance misuse services and a genuine commitment to helping people achieve meaningful, lasting change. You understand that recovery is different for everyone and can adapt your approach to meet individual needs, whether through harm reduction, abstinence-based support or a combination of both.

You will bring experience of conducting comprehensive assessments, developing risk management plans and implementing SMART care plans, alongside the ability to deliver structured psychosocial interventions and facilitate both individual and group sessions. You will be confident using motivational interviewing techniques to build trusting relationships, encourage engagement and support service users to take ownership of their recovery.

You will also have:
- A sound understanding of substance misuse, addiction, the recovery agenda and the challenges faced by individuals affected by drug and alcohol use.
- A thorough knowledge of, and commitment to, the 12-step process of recovery from addiction.
- An understanding of safeguarding, risk management, equality, diversity and inclusion, and the importance of delivering safe, accessible and person-centred services.
- Knowledge of community support services, holistic care needs and the importance of effective throughcare and continuity of care.
- An understanding of the criminal justice sector and the needs of individuals accessing support in community or prison settings.
- Experience of working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partner agencies to improve outcomes for service users.
- Strong IT, communication, organisational and record-keeping skills, with the ability to manage a caseload effectively and work towards agreed targets.
- An understanding of NHS health and wellbeing outcomes and the importance of measuring progress and demonstrating positive results.
- A commitment to reflective practice, professional development and making effective use of clinical supervision.

Above all, you will be non-judgemental, resilient and empathetic, with the ability to build positive relationships with people from diverse backgrounds. You will be passionate about promoting recovery, reducing harm, tackling health inequalities and helping individuals develop the confidence, skills and support networks they need to move forward with their lives.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

Please note that remote roles may require occasional travel for site visits, training and meetings.

description: This role support to deliver a comprehensive reception, administrative, and clerical service that supports the multidisciplinary team in providing patient care within the department. Additionally, to offer a welcoming and professional front-of-house experience for all patients and their families receiving care at The Princess Alexandra Hospital. The role is a fixed term contract until February 2027. The Ward Clerk provides an efficient, accurate and welcoming administrative service that supports the safe and smooth running of the ward. The post holder acts as a key point of contact for patients, relatives, carers, clinical teams and partner services; maintains complete and timely patient information; and supports admissions, transfers, discharge processes and day-to-day ward organisation. In a Care of the Elderly setting, the post holder will communicate patiently and respectfully with people who may be frail, anxious, hearing or visually impaired, living with dementia or delirium, or dependent on relatives and carers for support. The Ward Clerk will recognise the limits of the role, maintain confidentiality and promptly refer clinical questions, safeguarding concerns or changes in a person's condition to a registered practitioner. The Ward Clerk is a key member of the multidisciplinary team and is responsible for providing a comprehensive, efficient and professional administrative service to support the delivery of high-quality patient care within the ward environment. Acting as a central point of communication, the post holder will work closely with nursing, medical, therapy and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the ward. The post holder will be responsible for managing a wide range of administrative duties, including maintaining accurate patient information, supporting admission, transfer and discharge processes, preparing and filing documentation, and ensuring patient records are available and up to date. They will be expected to use a variety of electronic patient record systems and administrative databases, ensuring all information is entered accurately and in a timely manner. As the first point of contact for many patients, relatives and visitors, the Ward Clerk will provide a welcoming and professional reception service, responding to enquiries both in person and over the telephone. The role requires excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to deal sensitively and professionally with individuals who may be anxious, distressed or have additional communication needs. The post holder will ensure that enquiries are directed appropriately and that messages are communicated promptly and accurately to the relevant members of the clinical team. Working within a busy ward environment, the Ward Clerk will support the coordination of patient flow by assisting with admissions, bed moves, transfers and discharges. This includes preparing documentation, arranging transport where required, processing referrals and appointments, and liaising with internal and external departments to ensure patient journeys are managed efficiently. The role requires strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a varied workload while maintaining attention to detail. The post holder will provide administrative support to the wider multidisciplinary team, including preparing correspondence, photocopying, scanning and distributing documents, maintaining filing systems, ordering stationery and office supplies, and supporting ward meetings and operational activities as required. They will contribute to maintaining an organised, professional and efficient ward environment, ensuring administrative processes run smoothly and effectively. A significant aspect of the role involves working within a Care of the Elderly setting, supporting patients who may be frail, living with dementia, experiencing confusion or managing multiple long-term conditions. The post holder will be expected to demonstrate compassion, patience and understanding at all times, adapting their communication style to meet individual patient needs while maintaining dignity, privacy and respect. The Ward Clerk will be responsible for maintaining confidentiality and handling sensitive information in accordance with Trust policies, information governance standards and data protection legislation. They will ensure that all patient records, correspondence and documentation are managed securely and accurately, recognising the importance of high-quality information in supporting safe patient care. The post holder will contribute to maintaining quality and safety standards by complying with Trust policies and procedures, including infection prevention and control, health and safety, safeguarding and equality and diversity requirements.
